conversationMetrics.cachedSourceUnavailable: The cached analysis lacks verified speaker roles and the original credit before adjustment. Cached feedback is preserved; no new speed deduction is applied. Available segment gaps remain visible.

timingSource.word: Timing source: provider word timestamps. Speech estimates use word intervals; constructed segment durations include internal pauses.
timingSource.segment: Timing source: provider segment timestamps, not word timestamps. Duration, WPM and talk-share estimates include pauses within segments; they are not measurements of voiced speech.

conversationMetrics.providerSegmentCoverage: Segment timing coverage: {{excluded}} of {{total}} segments excluded; {{analyzed}} transcript tokens in analyzed segments. Individual word timings are unavailable.
conversationMetrics.segmentInterruptionsUnavailable: Interruptions and overlap duration are unavailable with segment timestamps. Segment overlaps do not establish whether an interruption occurred.
conversationMetrics.segmentLexicalEvidence: Filler and repetition matches come from segment text. Open the source segment and use its playback control; the exact word time is unknown.
conversationMetrics.deterministicOnly: Calculated measurements only. No model-generated interpretation was requested.

segmentMetrics.agentSpeechSeconds: Combined duration of the agent's usable provider segments, including pauses inside each segment. Overlapping intervals for the same speaker count once. This is an estimate of segment time, not voiced speech.
segmentMetrics.customerSpeechSeconds: Combined duration of the customer's usable provider segments, including pauses inside them, using the same interval method as the agent estimate.
segmentMetrics.overlapSeconds: Unavailable for segment timestamps. Overlap between diarized segments is not word-level overlap evidence and cannot establish interruption duration.
segmentMetrics.agentTalkPercent: Estimated agent segment time divided by agent plus customer segment time, multiplied by 100. Both estimates include internal pauses; this does not measure listening quality or the fraction of the recording with voiced agent speech.
segmentMetrics.longestAgentTurnSeconds: Longest stored agent turn estimate from provider segments, including internal pauses.
segmentMetrics.interruptionCandidateCount: Unavailable for segment timestamps. The system does not infer interruptions from provider segment overlaps, and an unavailable count must not be read as zero interruptions.
segmentMetrics.fillerCandidatesPer100Words: Agent lexical filler/repetition candidates divided by agent transcript-token count in usable segments, multiplied by 100. Individual words have no timing. This rate is not a quality score; check coverage before comparing calls.

providerSegments.segments: The provider supplies speaker-labeled text segments with start and end times. WPM uses each segment's transcript-token count and full duration, including pauses. No word timestamps are invented and numbers count as written tokens. Adjacent same-speaker segments may join for turn-duration estimates; speed eligibility remains segment-based.
providerSegments.evidence: Evidence links retain original segment boundaries. Filler and repetition matches are lexical candidates located somewhere inside the source segment; the evidence link selects the entire segment for transcript playback, not an invented word interval. Response gaps use the adjacent segment boundaries. Shown-versus-total counts describe display limits, not coverage.
providerSegments.coverage: Segment coverage counts excluded provider segments and transcript tokens in analyzed segments. These token counts are lexical text counts, not counts of validated word timestamps. Missing word timing does not make supported segment estimates unavailable.
providerSegments.partialCoverage: Excluded segments do not contribute to timing summaries. Response-gap and turn calculations do not bridge excluded spans. Unknown speaker roles are retained as evidence but do not establish agent or customer talk time. Read the current coverage warning; unshown evidence may still contribute, while excluded evidence does not.

help.title: Understanding conversation dynamics
help.intro: How measurements, evidence and the speed adjustment are interpreted.

metrics.fastSegmentCount: Stored count of agent segments classified as fast. Reference policy unavailable.
metrics.fastestWpm: Highest stored speaking-rate estimate among evaluated agent segments. Reference policy unavailable.
metrics.agentSpeechSeconds: Combined duration of the agent's measured word intervals. Overlapping intervals for that speaker count once; gaps between words are not counted as speech.
metrics.customerSpeechSeconds: Combined duration of the customer's measured word intervals, using the same method as the agent speech estimate.
metrics.overlapSeconds: Total duration where different speakers' word intervals overlap, without double-counting overlapping episodes. This does not establish who interrupted whom.
metrics.agentTalkPercent: Agent speech time divided by agent plus customer speech time, multiplied by 100. This is not a percentage of the recording duration: simultaneous speech contributes to both speakers' totals. It does not measure listening quality.
metrics.longestAgentTurnSeconds: Longest stored agent turn estimate, including internal pauses.
metrics.medianResponseGapSeconds: Median gap between consecutive segments from different speakers, in both directions. Positive values indicate a timestamp gap; negative values indicate overlap. These are not confirmed silence or hold times.
metrics.interruptionCandidateCount: Count of merged cross-speaker overlap episodes. The count can include brief acknowledgments and uncertain overlaps, not just possible interruptions. Review the recording; zero candidates does not prove that no interruption occurred.
metrics.fillerCandidateCount: Agent matches for eh, em, mmm, mm and pues, plus adjacent repeated words within a segment. These are contextual candidates, not automatically speech problems. Evidence can include other speakers, with their roles labeled.
metrics.fillerCandidatesPer100Words: Agent filler/repetition candidates divided by measured agent word count, multiplied by 100. This normalizes for sample length, but is not a quality score. Check coverage before comparing calls.

help.segments: Stored speaker segments retain transcript text and timing evidence. Reference segmentation policy unavailable.
help.formula: WPM = segment word count × 60 ÷ segment duration in seconds. Reference scoring policy unavailable.
help.fastExample: Speed classifications are stored analysis results.
help.exclusions: Reference exclusion policy unavailable. Stored base credit, actual deduction, final credit and reason remain available when present.
help.evidence: Expandable lists show speaking segments, overlap candidates, response gaps and filler/repetition candidates with timestamps and original excerpts. Playback buttons open the corresponding audio location when audio is available. Shown-versus-total counts describe the limited evidence display, not measurement coverage.
help.observations: A separate interpreter produces Spanish coaching observations from stored measurements and links them to evidence. It does not calculate or replace the measurements. Pending, unavailable or failed observations do not mean that completed rubric feedback failed. These estimates do not measure pitch, volume or emotion.
help.coverage: Word coverage counts provider word entries that passed validation, were excluded, or have unknown speaker roles. When segment coverage is present, read it too: a word can have valid individual timing while belonging to an excluded segment. Coverage values are specific to the current call.
help.statuses: Available means the required measurements can be supported. Partial means only some measurements or portions of timing evidence are usable. Unavailable means the required evidence is insufficient. A dash means unavailable, not zero. A measured zero only describes the evidence that was assessed.
help.truncationTitle: When the evidence display is limited
help.fullCoverageContext: For reports whose summary covers the full call, this message describes display limits rather than excluded timing:
help.partialCoverage: If timing segments are excluded, summaries cover only the retained usable evidence, not the full recording. With segment-level timing validation, a word with identical start/end timestamps excludes its whole segment from measurements; evidence remains visible. Transitions and overlaps touching excluded spans are suppressed, not joined across the missing evidence. Other malformed timing can still make results unavailable. Read the panel's coverage and exclusion warning. An excerpt limit and a timing exclusion are different: unseen rows may still contribute to a summary, but excluded timing does not.

conversationMetrics.truncated: Only part of the evidence is shown, with bounded excerpts and source references. Summary measurements cover the full call, not just the displayed rows.
conversationMetrics.truncatedRetained: Only part of the evidence is shown, with bounded excerpts and source references. Summary measurements cover retained timing-valid segments, including those not shown, but exclude segments with invalid timing.

conversationMetrics.noRetainedCandidates: No events detected in retained timing-valid evidence; excluded segments were not assessed.

conversationMetrics.interruptionCaution: Timestamp overlap candidates require listening verification. A brief acknowledgment may overlap without interrupting. No candidates does not prove no interruptions occurred.
conversationMetrics.gapCaution: Timestamp gaps are not confirmed silence or hold time. Negative gaps indicate overlap.
conversationMetrics.fillerCaution: Summary filler counts cover the agent only. Evidence may include other speakers, labeled by role. Lexical matches and repetitions are contextual candidates, not confirmed speech problems or grade deductions.
conversationMetrics.noCandidates: No events detected in the available evidence; this is not proof of absence in the recording.
